"""Checks the MNIST files fixed by Nix (IDX format) and shows samples of each digit."""
import tsugumi
import struct

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from card.dataset import DIRECTORY as directory, SOURCE as source  # written by default.nix
from tsugumi import Failure


def read_idx(path, magic, dims):
    """An IDX file: a big-endian magic number, the sizes, then one byte per value."""
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    head = struct.unpack(f">{1 + dims}I", data[:4 * (1 + dims)])
    if head[0] != magic:
        raise Failure("output_invalid", f"{path}: magic number {head[0]}, expected {magic}")
    values = np.frombuffer(data, dtype=np.uint8, offset=4 * (1 + dims))
    return values.reshape(head[1:])


def main(inputs, report):
    train_images = read_idx(f'{directory}/train-images-idx3-ubyte', 2051, 3)
    train_labels = read_idx(f'{directory}/train-labels-idx1-ubyte', 2049, 1)
    test_images = read_idx(f'{directory}/t10k-images-idx3-ubyte', 2051, 3)
    test_labels = read_idx(f'{directory}/t10k-labels-idx1-ubyte', 2049, 1)
    if train_images.shape != (60000, 28, 28) or test_images.shape != (10000, 28, 28):
        raise Failure("output_invalid", f"unexpected shapes {train_images.shape}, {test_images.shape}")
    if len(train_labels) != 60000 or len(test_labels) != 10000:
        raise Failure("output_invalid", "the label files do not match the image files")
    report.log(str(f"source: {source}"))
    report.log(str(f"train: {train_images.shape}, test: {test_images.shape}, directory: {directory}"))

    per_digit = 20
    rows = [np.hstack(test_images[test_labels == d][:per_digit]) for d in range(10)]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.4), layout="constrained")
    ax.imshow(np.vstack(rows), cmap="gray_r", vmin=0, vmax=255)
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(10) * 28 + 14, labels=range(10))
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.tick_params(length=0)
    ax.set_title(f"MNIST handwritten digits: {len(train_labels)} training, {len(test_labels)} test images\n"
                 f"The first {per_digit} test images of each digit. Source: {source}", fontsize=10)
    report.figure()
    directory_offset = directory
    source_offset = source
    _out_value = {}
    _out_value['directory'] = directory_offset
    _out_value['source'] = source_offset
    _out_value['train_count'] = len(train_labels)
    _out_value['test_count'] = len(test_labels)
    return {'dataset': _out_value}

"""Draws a stratified subset, scales the pixels to 0..1 and writes it for every classifier."""
import tsugumi
import hashlib
import os

import numpy as np

from inputs.dataset.mnist.Dataset import Dataset
from tsugumi import Failure


def read(path, header, shape=(-1,)):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        return np.frombuffer(f.read(), dtype=np.uint8, offset=header).reshape(shape)


def stratified(labels, size, rng):
    """`size` indices keeping the share of each digit (largest remainders round it)."""
    counts = np.bincount(labels, minlength=10)
    quota = size * counts / counts.sum()
    take = np.floor(quota).astype(int)
    take[np.argsort(take - quota, kind="stable")[: size - take.sum()]] += 1
    chosen = [rng.permutation(np.flatnonzero(labels == d))[: take[d]] for d in range(10)]
    return rng.permutation(np.concatenate(chosen))


def main(inputs, report, run):
    dataset = inputs.input("dataset", Dataset)
    directory = dataset.Directory().decode()
    params = inputs.params
    seed, train_size, test_size = params.seed, params.trainSize, params.testSize
    if not 10 <= train_size <= dataset.TrainCount() or not 10 <= test_size <= dataset.TestCount():
        raise Failure("output_invalid", f"train_size must be 10..{dataset.TrainCount()}, "
                                        f"test_size 10..{dataset.TestCount()}")

    all_train_x = read(f'{directory}/train-images-idx3-ubyte', 16, (-1, 784))
    all_train_y = read(f'{directory}/train-labels-idx1-ubyte', 8)
    all_test_x = read(f'{directory}/t10k-images-idx3-ubyte', 16, (-1, 784))
    all_test_y = read(f'{directory}/t10k-labels-idx1-ubyte', 8)

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    train = stratified(all_train_y, train_size, rng)
    test = stratified(all_test_y, test_size, rng)
    train_x = all_train_x[train].astype(np.float32) / 255
    test_x = all_test_x[test].astype(np.float32) / 255
    train_y, test_y = all_train_y[train], all_test_y[test]
    digest = hashlib.sha256(test_x.tobytes() + test_y.tobytes()).hexdigest()[:16]

    path = os.path.join(run.output_directory, "subset.npz")
    np.savez_compressed(path, train_images=train_x, train_labels=train_y,
                        test_images=test_x, test_labels=test_y, digest=digest)
    report.log(str(f"wrote {path}: {os.path.getsize(path)} bytes, test digest {digest}"))

    rows = [f"| {d} | {np.sum(all_train_y == d)} | {np.sum(train_y == d)} | "
            f"{np.sum(all_test_y == d)} | {np.sum(test_y == d)} |" for d in range(10)]
    report.markdown(
        f"**Stratified sample** seed {seed}: {train_size} training, {test_size} test images (keeping the share of each digit). "
        f"Pixels are 0–1, 784 dimensions.\n\n"
        "| Digit | Training (all) | Training (used) | Test (all) | Test (used) |\n| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n"
        + "\n".join(rows)
    )
    value = path
    _out_value = {}
    _out_value['value'] = value
    return {'subset': _out_value}

"""k nearest neighbours: a test digit takes the majority label of the k closest training digits."""
import tsugumi
import os

# One thread: the numbers repeat and the times compare. Before the imports: the libraries read it as they load.
os.environ["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"

import time

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier

from inputs.data.mnist.SubsetFile import SubsetFile


def confusions(ax, y, pred):
    """The mistakes only: true digit (rows) against predicted digit (columns)."""
    m = np.zeros((10, 10), dtype=int)
    np.add.at(m, (y, pred), 1)
    np.fill_diagonal(m, 0)
    ax.imshow(m, cmap="Reds")
    for i, j in zip(*np.nonzero(m)):
        ax.text(j, i, m[i, j], ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7, color="white" if m[i, j] > m.max() / 2 else "black")
    ax.set(xticks=range(10), yticks=range(10), xlabel="Predicted", ylabel="True", title="Breakdown of mistakes (images)")
    ax.tick_params(length=0, labelsize=8)


def send(inputs, name, settings, digest, y, pred, fit, predict):
    result_ports = {}
    model = name
    settings = settings
    digest = digest
    predictions = pred.astype(np.uint8)
    _out_value = {}
    _out_value['model'] = model
    _out_value['settings'] = settings
    _out_value['digest'] = digest
    _out_value['accuracy'] = float(np.mean(pred == y))
    _out_value['fit_seconds'] = fit
    _out_value['predict_seconds'] = predict
    _out_value['predictions'] = predictions
    result_ports.update({'result': _out_value})
    return result_ports


def main(inputs, report):
    result_ports = {}
    k = inputs.params.k
    data = np.load(inputs.input("data", SubsetFile).Value().decode())
    train_x, train_y, test_x, test_y = data["train_images"], data["train_labels"], data["test_images"], data["test_labels"]

    model = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=k, algorithm="brute")
    start = time.process_time()
    model.fit(train_x, train_y)
    fit = time.process_time() - start
    start = time.process_time()
    pred = model.predict(test_x)
    predict = time.process_time() - start
    accuracy = np.mean(pred == test_y)
    report.log(str(f"knn k={k}: accuracy {accuracy:.4f}, fit {fit:.3f} s, predict {predict:.3f} s"))

    # What it did on a few mistakes: the test digit, then its nearest training digits.
    wrong = np.flatnonzero(pred != test_y)[:6]
    shown = min(k, 4)
    neighbours = model.kneighbors(test_x[wrong], n_neighbors=shown, return_distance=False)
    rows = [np.hstack([test_x[w].reshape(28, 28)] + [train_x[n].reshape(28, 28) for n in ns])
            for w, ns in zip(wrong, neighbours)]

    fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 4.2), layout="constrained")
    confusions(left, test_y, pred)
    if rows:
        right.imshow(np.vstack(rows), cmap="gray_r")
    for row, w in enumerate(wrong):
        right.text(-3, 28 * row + 14, f"true {test_y[w]} → {pred[w]}", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=8)
    right.set_xticks(28 * np.arange(1 + shown) + 14, labels=["Test"] + [f"Neighbour {i + 1}" for i in range(shown)], fontsize=8)
    right.set_yticks([])
    right.tick_params(length=0)
    right.set_title("Digits it got wrong, and their neighbours")
    fig.suptitle(f"k-nearest neighbours k={k}: accuracy {accuracy:.4f}, training {fit:.2f} s, prediction {predict:.2f} s", fontsize=11)
    report.figure()

    result_ports.update(send(inputs, 'knn', f'k={k}', str(data['digest']), test_y, pred, fit, predict))
    return result_ports

"""Gradient boosting: each round adds small trees that correct what the earlier ones got wrong."""
import tsugumi
import os

# One thread: the numbers repeat and the times compare. Before the imports: the libraries read it as they load.
os.environ["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"

import time

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import xgboost as xgb

from inputs.data.mnist.SubsetFile import SubsetFile


def confusions(ax, y, pred):
    """The mistakes only: true digit (rows) against predicted digit (columns)."""
    m = np.zeros((10, 10), dtype=int)
    np.add.at(m, (y, pred), 1)
    np.fill_diagonal(m, 0)
    ax.imshow(m, cmap="Reds")
    for i, j in zip(*np.nonzero(m)):
        ax.text(j, i, m[i, j], ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7, color="white" if m[i, j] > m.max() / 2 else "black")
    ax.set(xticks=range(10), yticks=range(10), xlabel="Predicted", ylabel="True", title="Breakdown of mistakes (images)")
    ax.tick_params(length=0, labelsize=8)


def send(inputs, name, settings, digest, y, pred, fit, predict):
    result_ports = {}
    model = name
    settings = settings
    digest = digest
    predictions = pred.astype(np.uint8)
    _out_value = {}
    _out_value['model'] = model
    _out_value['settings'] = settings
    _out_value['digest'] = digest
    _out_value['accuracy'] = float(np.mean(pred == y))
    _out_value['fit_seconds'] = fit
    _out_value['predict_seconds'] = predict
    _out_value['predictions'] = predictions
    result_ports.update({'result': _out_value})
    return result_ports


def main(inputs, report):
    result_ports = {}
    params = inputs.params
    rounds, max_depth, eta, seed = params.rounds, params.maxDepth, params.eta, params.seed
    data = np.load(inputs.input("data", SubsetFile).Value().decode())
    train_x, train_y, test_x, test_y = data["train_images"], data["train_labels"], data["test_images"], data["test_labels"]

    settings = {"objective": "multi:softprob", "num_class": 10, "max_depth": max_depth, "eta": eta,
                "tree_method": "hist", "max_bin": 64, "nthread": 1, "seed": seed}
    train = xgb.DMatrix(train_x, label=train_y)
    test = xgb.DMatrix(test_x)
    start = time.process_time()
    model = xgb.train(settings, train, num_boost_round=rounds)
    fit = time.process_time() - start
    start = time.process_time()
    pred = model.predict(test).argmax(axis=1)
    predict = time.process_time() - start
    accuracy = np.mean(pred == test_y)
    report.log(str(f"boosting rounds={rounds} depth={max_depth} eta={eta}: accuracy {accuracy:.4f}, fit {fit:.3f} s, predict {predict:.3f} s"))

    # The test error after each round, read back from the finished model (outside the timers).
    upto = np.unique(np.geomspace(1, rounds, 20).astype(int))
    errors = [np.mean(model.predict(test, iteration_range=(0, int(i))).argmax(axis=1) != test_y) for i in upto]

    fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 4.2), layout="constrained")
    confusions(left, test_y, pred)
    right.plot(upto, errors, marker="o", markersize=3, color="#c0392b")
    right.set(xlabel="Rounds", ylabel="Test error rate", ylim=(0, None), title="More rounds, fewer mistakes")
    right.grid(alpha=0.3)

"""A multilayer perceptron: two fully connected hidden layers, trained on the CPU with a fixed seed."""
import tsugumi
import os

# One thread: the numbers repeat and the times compare. Before the imports: the libraries read it as they load.
os.environ["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"

import time

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import nn

from inputs.data.mnist.SubsetFile import SubsetFile

BATCH = 64


def confusions(ax, y, pred):
    """The mistakes only: true digit (rows) against predicted digit (columns)."""
    m = np.zeros((10, 10), dtype=int)
    np.add.at(m, (y, pred), 1)
    np.fill_diagonal(m, 0)
    ax.imshow(m, cmap="Reds")
    for i, j in zip(*np.nonzero(m)):
        ax.text(j, i, m[i, j], ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7, color="white" if m[i, j] > m.max() / 2 else "black")
    ax.set(xticks=range(10), yticks=range(10), xlabel="Predicted", ylabel="True", title="Breakdown of mistakes (images)")
    ax.tick_params(length=0, labelsize=8)


def send(inputs, name, settings, digest, y, pred, fit, predict):
    result_ports = {}
    model = name
    settings = settings
    digest = digest
    predictions = pred.astype(np.uint8)
    _out_value = {}
    _out_value['model'] = model
    _out_value['settings'] = settings
    _out_value['digest'] = digest
    _out_value['accuracy'] = float(np.mean(pred == y))
    _out_value['fit_seconds'] = fit
    _out_value['predict_seconds'] = predict
    _out_value['predictions'] = predictions
    result_ports.update({'result': _out_value})
    return result_ports


def main(inputs, report):
    result_ports = {}
    params = inputs.params
    hidden, epochs, seed = params.hidden, params.epochs, params.seed
    data = np.load(inputs.input("data", SubsetFile).Value().decode())
    test_y = data["test_labels"]
    train_x = torch.from_numpy(data["train_images"])
    train_y = torch.from_numpy(data["train_labels"]).long()
    test_x = torch.from_numpy(data["test_images"])

    torch.set_num_threads(1)
    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
    generator = torch.manual_seed(seed)
    model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(784, hidden), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(hidden, hidden), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(hidden, 10))
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

    losses = []
    start = time.process_time()
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        order = torch.randperm(len(train_x), generator=generator)
        total = 0.0
        for i in range(0, len(order), BATCH):
            batch = order[i:i + BATCH]
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss = loss_fn(model(train_x[batch]), train_y[batch])
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            total += loss.item() * len(batch)
        losses.append(total / len(order))
        report.log(str(f"epoch {epoch + 1}: train loss {losses[-1]:.4f}"))
    fit = time.process_time() - start

    start = time.process_time()
    with torch.no_grad():
        pred = model(test_x).argmax(dim=1).numpy()
    predict = time.process_time() - start
    accuracy = np.mean(pred == test_y)
    report.log(str(f"mlp hidden={hidden} epochs={epochs}: accuracy {accuracy:.4f}, fit {fit:.3f} s, predict {predict:.3f} s"))

    fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 4.2), layout="constrained")
    confusions(left, test_y, pred)
    right.plot(range(1, epochs + 1), losses, marker="o", markersize=3, color="#c0392b")
    right.set(xlabel="Epoch", ylabel="Loss on the training data", ylim=(0, None), title="How training went")
    right.grid(alpha=0.3)
    fig.suptitle(f"MLP, width {hidden} × 2 layers, {epochs} epochs: accuracy {accuracy:.4f}, training {fit:.2f} s, prediction {predict:.3f} s", fontsize=11)
    report.figure()

    result_ports.update(send(inputs, 'mlp', f'hidden={hidden}, epochs={epochs}', str(data['digest']), test_y, pred, fit, predict))
    return result_ports

"""A small convolutional network: it sees the digit as an image, trained on the CPU with a fixed seed."""
import tsugumi
import os

# One thread: the numbers repeat and the times compare. Before the imports: the libraries read it as they load.
os.environ["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"

import time

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import nn

from inputs.data.mnist.SubsetFile import SubsetFile

BATCH = 64


def confusions(ax, y, pred):
    """The mistakes only: true digit (rows) against predicted digit (columns)."""
    m = np.zeros((10, 10), dtype=int)
    np.add.at(m, (y, pred), 1)
    np.fill_diagonal(m, 0)
    ax.imshow(m, cmap="Reds")
    for i, j in zip(*np.nonzero(m)):
        ax.text(j, i, m[i, j], ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7, color="white" if m[i, j] > m.max() / 2 else "black")
    ax.set(xticks=range(10), yticks=range(10), xlabel="Predicted", ylabel="True", title="Breakdown of mistakes (images)")
    ax.tick_params(length=0, labelsize=8)


def send(inputs, name, settings, digest, y, pred, fit, predict):
    result_ports = {}
    model = name
    settings = settings
    digest = digest
    predictions = pred.astype(np.uint8)
    _out_value = {}
    _out_value['model'] = model
    _out_value['settings'] = settings
    _out_value['digest'] = digest
    _out_value['accuracy'] = float(np.mean(pred == y))
    _out_value['fit_seconds'] = fit
    _out_value['predict_seconds'] = predict
    _out_value['predictions'] = predictions
    result_ports.update({'result': _out_value})
    return result_ports


def main(inputs, report):
    result_ports = {}
    params = inputs.params
    channels, epochs, seed = params.channels, params.epochs, params.seed
    data = np.load(inputs.input("data", SubsetFile).Value().decode())
    test_y = data["test_labels"]
    train_x = torch.from_numpy(data["train_images"]).reshape(-1, 1, 28, 28)
    train_y = torch.from_numpy(data["train_labels"]).long()
    test_x = torch.from_numpy(data["test_images"]).reshape(-1, 1, 28, 28)

    torch.set_num_threads(1)
    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
    generator = torch.manual_seed(seed)
    model = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Conv2d(1, channels, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(2),
        nn.Conv2d(channels, 2 * channels, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(2),
        nn.Flatten(), nn.Linear(2 * channels * 7 * 7, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, 10),
    )
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

    losses = []
    start = time.process_time()
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        order = torch.randperm(len(train_x), generator=generator)
        total = 0.0
        for i in range(0, len(order), BATCH):
            batch = order[i:i + BATCH]
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss = loss_fn(model(train_x[batch]), train_y[batch])
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            total += loss.item() * len(batch)
        losses.append(total / len(order))
        report.log(str(f"epoch {epoch + 1}: train loss {losses[-1]:.4f}"))
    fit = time.process_time() - start

    start = time.process_time()
    with torch.no_grad():
        pred = model(test_x).argmax(dim=1).numpy()
    predict = time.process_time() - start
    accuracy = np.mean(pred == test_y)
    report.log(str(f"cnn channels={channels} epochs={epochs}: accuracy {accuracy:.4f}, fit {fit:.3f} s, predict {predict:.3f} s"))

    # What the first layer picks out of one test digit, one small image per filter.
    with torch.no_grad():
        maps = model[0](test_x[:1])[0].numpy()
    columns = int(np.ceil(np.sqrt(len(maps))))
    canvas = np.full((columns * 29 - 1, columns * 29 - 1), np.nan)
    for n, activation in enumerate(maps):
        row, column = n // columns, n % columns
        canvas[row * 29:row * 29 + 28, column * 29:column * 29 + 28] = activation
    limit = np.abs(maps).max()

    fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 4.2), layout="constrained")
    confusions(left, test_y, pred)
    right.imshow(canvas, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-limit, vmax=limit)
    right.set(xticks=[], yticks=[], title=f"What the first layer's {len(maps)} filters pick out of the digit {test_y[0]}")
    fig.suptitle(f"CNN, {channels} channels, {epochs} epochs: accuracy {accuracy:.4f}, training {fit:.2f} s, prediction {predict:.3f} s", fontsize=11)
    report.figure()

    result_ports.update(send(inputs, 'cnn', f'channels={channels}, epochs={epochs}', str(data['digest']), test_y, pred, fit, predict))
    return result_ports

"""Waits for every branch, checks they scored the same test digits, and ranks them."""
import tsugumi
import numpy as np

# All seven branches send the same table, so one generated class reads them all.
from inputs.knn.mnist.Result import Result
from inputs.data.mnist.SubsetFile import SubsetFile
from tsugumi import Failure

MODELS = ["knn", "logistic", "svm", "forest", "boosting", "mlp", "cnn"]


def main(inputs, report):
    data = np.load(inputs.input("data", SubsetFile).Value().decode())
    labels = data["test_labels"]
    results = [inputs.input(m, Result) for m in MODELS]
    predictions = np.stack([r.PredictionsAsNumpy() for r in results])

    # The checks: same test digits, and each reported accuracy recomputed here.
    for m, r, pred in zip(MODELS, results, predictions):
        if r.Digest().decode() != str(data["digest"]):
            raise Failure("output_invalid", f"{m} was scored on other test digits: run it again")
        if abs(np.mean(pred == labels) - r.Accuracy()) > 1e-12:
            raise Failure("output_invalid", f"{m} reports {r.Accuracy()}, its predictions give {np.mean(pred == labels)}")

    accuracy = np.array([r.Accuracy() for r in results])
    fit = np.array([r.FitSeconds() for r in results])
    predict = np.array([r.PredictSeconds() for r in results])
    settings = [r.Settings().decode() for r in results]
    n = len(labels)
    order = np.argsort(-accuracy, kind="stable")

    rows = [f"| {rank + 1} | **{MODELS[i]}** | {accuracy[i]:.4f} | {fit[i]:.2f} | {predict[i]:.3f} | {settings[i]} |"
            for rank, i in enumerate(order)]
    best, second = order[0], order[1]
    # Two models scored on the same digits: what separates them is the digits only one gets right.
    only_best = int(np.sum((predictions[best] == labels) & (predictions[second] != labels)))
    only_second = int(np.sum((predictions[best] != labels) & (predictions[second] == labels)))
    disagree = only_best + only_second
    margin = accuracy[best] - accuracy[second]
    noise = np.sqrt(disagree) / n
    verdict = (f"The difference {margin:.4f}, against the fluctuation expected from the {disagree} images on which the two disagree (about {noise:.4f}), "
               + ("is at least twice that, so even with this many images there is a difference." if margin >= 2 * noise else
                  "does not reach twice that, so with this many images the order cannot be decided."))
    se = np.sqrt(accuracy[best] * (1 - accuracy[best]) / n)
    fastest_fit = np.argmin(fit)
    fastest_predict = np.argmin(predict)
    report.markdown(
        f"**Compared on {n} test images** (the same images for all; accuracies recomputed from the predictions and confirmed)\n\n"
        "| Rank | Model | Accuracy | Training (s) | Prediction (s) | Settings |\n| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |\n"
        + "\n".join(rows)
        + f"\n\nThe highest accuracy is **{MODELS[best]}** ({accuracy[best]:.4f}, standard error about {se:.4f}), "
          f"followed by **{MODELS[second]}** ({accuracy[second]:.4f}). {verdict}\n\n"
          f"The shortest training is **{MODELS[fastest_fit]}** ({fit[fastest_fit]:.2f} s), "
          f"The shortest prediction is **{MODELS[fastest_predict]}** ({predict[fastest_predict]:.3f} s)."
          "Times are single-thread CPU times and vary by machine."
    )
    names = [m for m in MODELS]
    _b_items = []
    for name in reversed(names):
        _b_items.append(name)
    models_offset = list(reversed(_b_items))
    accuracy_offset = accuracy
    fit_offset = fit
    predict_offset = predict
    labels_offset = labels
    predictions_offset = predictions.ravel()
    images = np.round(data["test_images"].ravel() * 255).astype(np.uint8)
    images_offset = images
    _out_value = {}
    _out_value['models'] = models_offset
    _out_value['accuracy'] = accuracy_offset
    _out_value['fit_seconds'] = fit_offset
    _out_value['predict_seconds'] = predict_offset
    _out_value['test_labels'] = labels_offset
    _out_value['predictions'] = predictions_offset
    _out_value['test_images'] = images_offset
    return {'comparison': _out_value}

"""Per-digit recall of every model: which digit is hard, and for whom."""
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from inputs.comparison.mnist.Comparison import Comparison


def main(inputs, report):
    c = inputs.input("comparison", Comparison)
    models = [c.Models(i).decode() for i in range(c.ModelsLength())]
    accuracy = c.AccuracyAsNumpy()
    labels = c.TestLabelsAsNumpy()
    predictions = c.PredictionsAsNumpy().reshape(len(models), len(labels))

    order = np.argsort(-accuracy, kind="stable")
    recall = np.array([[np.mean(predictions[m][labels == d] == d) for d in range(10)] for m in order])
    mean_by_digit = recall.mean(axis=0)
    hardest, easiest = np.argmin(mean_by_digit), np.argmax(mean_by_digit)
    report.log(" ".join(str(value) for value in ("mean recall by digit:", np.round(mean_by_digit, 4).tolist(),)))

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.4), layout="constrained")
    image = ax.imshow(recall, cmap="viridis", vmin=recall.min(), vmax=1, aspect="auto")
    for i in range(recall.shape[0]):
        for j in range(10):
            mid = (recall.min() + 1) / 2
            ax.text(j, i, f"{recall[i, j]:.3f}".lstrip("0"), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9,
                    color="black" if recall[i, j] > mid else "white")
    ax.set_xticks(range(10), labels=range(10))
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(order)), labels=[models[m] for m in order])
    ax.set_xlabel("True digit")
    ax.tick_params(length=0)
    ax.set_title(f"Recall per digit. The hardest is {hardest} (mean {mean_by_digit[hardest]:.3f}), "
                 f"the easiest is {easiest} (mean {mean_by_digit[easiest]:.3f})", fontsize=11)
    fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, shrink=0.8, label="Recall")
    report.figure()

"""The test digits most models get wrong, with what those models said instead."""
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from inputs.comparison.mnist.Comparison import Comparison

SHOWN = 32


def main(inputs, report):
    c = inputs.input("comparison", Comparison)
    n_models = c.ModelsLength()
    labels = c.TestLabelsAsNumpy()
    predictions = c.PredictionsAsNumpy().reshape(n_models, len(labels))
    images = c.TestImagesAsNumpy().reshape(len(labels), 28, 28)

    wrong = (predictions != labels).sum(axis=0)
    order = np.argsort(-wrong, kind="stable")[:SHOWN]
    counts = np.bincount(wrong, minlength=n_models + 1)
    report.log(" ".join(str(value) for value in ("test digits by the number of models wrong:", counts.tolist(),)))

    columns = 8
    rows = int(np.ceil(len(order) / columns))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, columns, figsize=(8, 1.25 * rows + 0.9), layout="constrained")
    for ax in axes.ravel():
        ax.axis("off")
    for ax, i in zip(axes.ravel(), order):
        answers = np.bincount(predictions[predictions[:, i] != labels[i], i], minlength=10)
        ax.imshow(images[i], cmap="gray_r")
        ax.set_title(f"{labels[i]} → {answers.argmax()}  ({wrong[i]}/{n_models})" if wrong[i] else f"{labels[i]}", fontsize=8)
    fig.suptitle(f"Test images many models got wrong (true → the most common wrong answer, number of models wrong)\n"
                 f"Of {len(labels)} images, all {n_models} models got {counts[0]} right and all got {counts[n_models]} wrong",
                 fontsize=10)
    report.figure()

notes.html:
Telling handwritten digits apart seven ways

The same MNIST subset goes to seven classifiers, each trained at the same time in its own Nix environment, and they are compared at the end on the same test images.

accuracy=1N∑i=1N1[y^i=yi],SE≈p(1−p)N\mathrm{accuracy} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathbf{1}[\hat y_i = y_i], \qquad \mathrm{SE} \approx \sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)}{N}}

Read differences in accuracy against the error SE set by the number of test images NN. Times are single-thread CPU times and vary by machine.

Try: change a parameter of a classifier Card (k of knn, max_depth of forest, epochs of cnn and so on) and run just that Card; the other branches do not move, and only that Card's display changes. To compare again, run from that Card onwards. compare compares the new result with the saved inputs of the other branches, so the accuracies of the branches you did not change stay the same. How many Cards run at once is "Parallel runs" in the settings (4 by default).

The default counts are not the whole set (10000 training, 2000 test). To compare with published figures, increase the counts in prepare.

Plots accuracy against time with Plotly.

The highest accuracy is svm (0.9705, standard error about 0.0038), followed by cnn (0.9640). The difference 0.0065, against the fluctuation expected from the 75 images on which the two disagree (about 0.0043), does not reach twice that, so with this many images the order cannot be decided.

intro: A demo that feeds the real MNIST to seven classifiers at once and compares accuracy and time. Each classifier has its own Nix environment.
finale: The seven results are lined up on the same footing. In the app you can change one classifier's settings and rerun just that branch.
